decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 50 basis points, to 5.5%.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee at its meeting today decided to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 5-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 6 percent.”

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 50 basis point reduction in the discount rate to 5 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 25-basis-point decrease in the discount rate to 5-3/4 percent, the level requested by seven Reserve Banks…”

changes.quote: Consumer and business confidence has eroded further, exacerbated by rising energy costs that continue to drain consumer purchasing power and press on business profit margins.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Partly as a consequence, retail sales and business spending on capital equipment have weakened appreciably.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: In response, manufacturing production has been cut back sharply, with new technologies appearing to have accelerated the response of production and demand to potential excesses in the stock of inventories and capital equipment.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Taken together, and with inflation contained, these circumstances have called for a rapid and forceful response of monetary policy.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: Nonetheless, the Committee continues to believe that against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.
The Federal Open Market Committee at its meeting today decided to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 5-1/2 percent.

In response, manufacturing production has been cut back sharply, with new technologies appearing to have accelerated the response of production and demand to potential excesses in the stock of inventories and capital equipment.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.98% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.19% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.02% would fall by about $10.07 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 126k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.4% over the past year (December 2000); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -8 bp on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates).
